A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAFE-SQL. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spider execution-accuracy results, component ablations, filtering analyses and appendix experiments on model size and cross-model example generation.

after.justification: v2 retains original Spider experiments and reports additional BIRD results, model configurations and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: Schema linking, generation of ten examples, three-component relevance scoring, selection at threshold 8 and final in-context inference remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies LLM scoring already documented in v1 Appendix B.2; the appendix prompt edits do not establish a substantive procedural change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only Spider. v2 adds BIRD development-set evaluation, introducing a second cross-domain collection of database schemas and question-SQL pairs into the empirical coverage (Sections 4.1 and 4.4, Table 2).

E2.justification: The competing methods in Spider Table 1 remain SYN-SQL, SQL-Palm, zero-shot baselines, C3-SQL, DIN-SQL, DAIL-SQL, ACT-SQL, PTD-SQL and DEA-SQL. BIRD uses the same comparator set. C3q-SQL becomes C3-SQL; additional model rows are SAFE-SQL configurations.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations change substantially: v1 Appendix D.1's GPT-4o-generated examples with small inference models disappear, while v2 adds Llama3.1/3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B and Gemma3-12B/27B evaluations. Per-query inference time becomes an additional metric. Spider's EX/EM definitions and the appendix Qwen3B/7B/14B study remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a measured inference-time comparison and removes Appendix D.1's investigation of whether GPT-4o-generated and filtered examples improve smaller inference models. The component ablations, threshold and weighting analyses, embedding analyses, case study and Qwen model-size study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained correlation analysis and its reporting practice are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds BIRD results, including 63.5% EX for SAFE-SQL with GPT-4o, five new Spider model rows, including 88.5% for Gemma3-27B, and timing values. Spider DAIL-SQL overall EX changes from 83.1 to 83.6, while the original SAFE-SQL GPT results remain unchanged. v1 Appendix D.1's four hybrid-model result rows are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1 and 2 retain the weighted relevance score, weights summing to one and thresholded example-set definition. Revised component descriptions explain the existing appendix rubric. No theorems, proofs or substantive derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an unsupervised framework that generates and filters demonstrations without additional fine-tuning or predefined training examples, improving execution accuracy particularly on difficult and unseen queries. Reworded abstracts, contribution bullets and conclusions retain these claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations emphasizing open-model cost-effectiveness and describing the latency increase from three LLM calls as worthwhile. Removing Appendix D.1 also removes its specific discussion of small models' example-generation limitations and GPT-4o assistance. The dedicated Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 analysis checkpoint identifier and Appendix D.1's explicit generation/filtering versus final-inference model assignment. It newly states three LLM calls, reports timing values and shortens the final-inference prompt. Timing units and measurement conditions are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the fine-tuning, retrieval, decomposition and self-correction survey with positioning around schema information and example augmentation/filtering. It adds RAT-SQL, Self-Instruct, demonstration-selection and reasoning-prompt literature while removing discussion and citations of AST-SQL, SelECT-SQL, MAGIC and several other works.

P1.justification: Section 2 is extensively rewritten and restructured, and Section 3.3 replaces worked-example explanations with a clearer rubric-based description. The abstract, conclusion and contribution bullets are rewritten, terminology is standardized, appendix prompts are edited and the author list changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains model rows and a Time column, a BIRD table is added, and v1's final appendix model table is removed. Figure 2 gains numbered stages; captions, table headings, prompt formatting and float positions change. The overall two-column layout and existing analytical plots are retained.

improvement.justification: BIRD evaluation provides evidence that the accuracy advantage extends beyond v1's sole Spider benchmark, and the revised scoring explanation improves clarity. These gains are tempered by removal of the useful cross-model transfer study and exact checkpoint information. Timing results add practical evidence, but missing units and measurement conditions limit their value.
